orders: Slit lamp examination of both irides for sectoral sphincter palsy
Test the affected pupil's near response to assess for light-near dissociation
Cover-uncover test and full extraocular movement assessment in all nine positions of gaze
Instill pilocarpine 0.125% in the affected eye and observe for constriction over 30–45 minutes
If no response, instill pilocarpine 1% in the affected eye and observe for constriction
Measure intraocular pressure in both eyes
Best-corrected visual acuity and colour vision testing (Ishihara) in both eyes
Urgent MRI of the brain with contrast and MRA of the circle of Willis

dx_raw:
**DIAGNOSIS:** Right Adie (tonic) pupil in the paretic phase, with concurrent right pupil-involving oculomotor (third) nerve palsy, most likely due to shared microvascular (ischaemic) aetiology

1. Idiopathic right pupil-involving oculomotor nerve palsy with coincidental Adie tonic pupil
2. Posterior communicating artery aneurysm (clinically excluded by negative CTA/MRA, but small compressive lesion cannot be entirely ruled out)
3. Inflammatory/infiltrative oculomotor neuropathy (e.g. GCA, sarcoidosis, meningitis) with associated tonic pupil changes
